prototype_feel_reasons: On mobile, the horizontally oversized scene is clipped at the viewport edge, cutting the right-side character and workstation mid-body.
The hotspot label and magnifier occupy a large portion of the left workstation, obscuring the chair and clipboard/tool area.
The hotspot’s stacked icon-and-label treatment feels bulky relative to the scene and competes with the illustrated subjects.
The desktop layout uses a narrow fixed-width play column surrounded by substantial empty space, making the composition feel insufficiently adapted for desktop.
issues: mobile/scene image — right-side character and workstation are cut by the viewport — provide a deliberate scroll viewport with stronger edge affordance and initialize object-position so no face or key workstation is stranded at the edge
studio hotspot — magnifier badge and text label obscure the chair and clipboard/tool area — move the label into lower-left floor space or use a leader line from a smaller marker
studio hotspot — marker and label visually dominate the nearby subject — reduce overlay scale and padding while preserving tap-target size with a transparent hit area

desktop/main composition — fixed narrow column leaves excessive unused canvas and makes the asset feel like a mobile prototype centered on desktop — use a wider responsive stage or add balanced surrounding UI framing
